clips.text: What if your bones were hollow like a bird's? You'd expect to float away. You wouldn't lose a single pound.
A two-ounce songbird's skeleton weighs exactly what a two-ounce mouse's weighs. Same size. Same weight.
The real superpower is stranger. A bird's lungs reach into its bones, so it breathes fresh air on the inhale AND the exhale.
But those hollow bones hold air, not marrow. And your marrow makes two hundred billion red blood cells a day.
No marrow, no new blood. Your cells live a hundred and twenty days. Then the tank reads empty.
Give yourself bird bones and you'd expect to float away. You wouldn't lose a single pound — but your blood factory would start a 120-day countdown.
